correctness.rationale: A geometric fixed point has invariant support and its weights on each edge orbit are constant. The simplex map sending an orbit to its barycenter has inverse given by summing weights, so it gives the claimed PL homeomorphism, not merely the complex of fixed vertices. A disjoint collection of occupied antipodal columns extends to a perfect matching by filling the unused columns with their spokes. The intersection of any chosen spoke stars consists exactly of faces that can be joined with the whole chosen spoke set; spokes never conflict with one another. This intersection is a nonempty cone, and the full nerve makes the union B contractible. Any face outside B has no spokes and covers every column by dimers; odd cyclic length has none and even cyclic length at least four has exactly the two alternating tilings. Their proper faces free columns and lie in B. Collapsing B is a homotopy equivalence because it is a contractible subcomplex, and the quotient is a wedge of two spheres of dimension n/2−1. For n=2 the separate rim choices and the spoke edge give three components, as claimed. Agarwal–Basak's Main Theorem 1(b) gives the same ambient even homotopy type, hence total mod-two Betti number 3 in both spaces; part (c) gives nontrivial sphere wedges for odd n≥3. The finite total 1966 including empty faces also checks independently: for each n=2,…,8 sum n·binom(n−k,k)·2^(n−2k)/(n−k) over k≤n/2, counting a k-dimer placement and a subset of the remaining spokes, with both parallel choices at n=2.
residual_risks: Equality of Betti totals is not a theorem about the induced map of the inclusion. This concerns the half-turn, not other subgroups or reflections.

checked_sources: Agarwal–Basak Main Theorem 1 and prior antipodal Lefschetz calculation
value.rationale: The half-turn is the central natural involution on the ladder. A complete fixed-point classification separates two genuinely different parity regimes, including contractible fixed points in ambient noncontractible wedges and an exact infinite family of Smith equalities. The homotopy argument retains information not contained in the earlier trace computations.
residual_risks: Does not classify reflection actions, all dihedral fixed spaces, or the equivariant homotopy type.
